routes.description: Establish first-person qualitative consciousness as irreducible data, show that quantitative physical descriptions cannot intelligibly derive its character, and present a consciousness-first ontology capable of grounding physical structure while remaining compatible with established empirical findings.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the explanatory limits attributed to physicalism support treating consciousness as fundamental and if the proposed consciousness-first account integrates qualitative experience with physical structure without forfeiting the relevant scientific constraints.

motionBridge.description: Connect physicalism's alleged inability to derive qualitative experience with a positive account on which consciousness grounds the physical structure described by science.

centralBridges.description: Establish conscious experience as independently known evidence that a complete theory of reality must accommodate.
Show why quantitative neural and physical descriptions do not by themselves make qualitative character intelligible.
Explain how a conscious intrinsic basis could realize the mathematical and relational structure identified by physics.
Show why empirical equivalence permits comparison by simplicity and explanatory coverage, including both experience and physical structure.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Preserve a causal or realizing role for consciousness against zombie-based and empirical-inertness objections.
Address compatibility with established physics and the challenge of combining simple conscious entities into unified subjects.

routes.description: Defend consciousness as a real higher-level feature instantiated by physical organization, specify a multilevel empirical explanation connecting brain states, experience, behavior, and dynamics, and show why adding fundamental consciousness does not improve on the constrained physical account.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if higher-level physical description can account for conscious experience without new fundamental ontology and if consciousness-first alternatives either conflict with established physical constraints or fail to add explanatory and causal consequences.

motionBridge.description: Connect weak emergence and multilevel physical explanation to a complete account of consciousness that requires no additional fundamental conscious entities.

centralBridges.description: Establish that conscious concepts can be valid higher-level descriptions of systems wholly constituted by physical processes.
Specify how mappings among physical states, experience, behavior, and dynamics could constitute an explanation of consciousness.
Use the tested physical account of human-scale interactions to constrain proposals that add or alter fundamental ontology.
Require a consciousness-first theory either to identify consequential changes to physics or explain what unchanged fundamental consciousness adds.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Show that private qualitative evidence can be included within broad empirical inquiry without establishing nonphysical fundamentals.
Relate consciousness to physical organization and behavior while addressing zombie and causal-irrelevance arguments.

sections.title: Qualitative Experience and the Scope of Physical Explanation
sections.rationale: This issue tests the central physicalist burden: whether quantitative neural descriptions and multilevel mappings can explain what experience is like, including the knowledge argument and the claimed explanatory gap.

sections.title: Emergence versus Consciousness-First Grounding
sections.rationale: This issue compares the rival motion-level accounts: consciousness as a higher-level physical description and consciousness as the intrinsic basis that realizes physical structure.

sections.title: Empirical Constraints and Theoretical Consequences
sections.rationale: This issue determines how each ontology relates to established physics and whether preserving or changing physical dynamics supplies explanatory, causal, or testable consequences.

sections.title: First-Person Data and the Method of Inquiry
sections.rationale: This issue addresses whether private conscious awareness requires philosophical synthesis beyond physical science or can be incorporated within an appropriately broad empirical method.

sections.title: Causation, Zombies, and the Unity of Consciousness
sections.rationale: This issue covers supporting burdens concerning consciousness's role in behavior, the implications of physically identical duplicates, multiple realization, and the formation of unified subjects from simpler conscious bases.
